title: Sessionization & credits — loose math + hypotheses
content:
Quick notes / stream-of-consciousness about session-based credits and a hybrid per-token+per-session billing idea.

Context / motivation:
- We want a pricing construct that (a) aligns with interactive UX (chat apps with many short sessions), (b) protects against abuse/very long tails, and (c) keeps simple unit economics for sales and finance.
- Starter credits and free tiers currently get blown by long-lived session state (users who keep sending short messages but the KV cache still counts).

Assumptions (base for all calcs):
- Model cost to Redwood (amortized tokens processed + GPU ops + infra overhead) ~ $0.00025 per token served for an average production mix (this is a placeholder; engineering to validate).
- Median message length: 15 tokens (user) + 45 tokens (model) = 60 tokens per roundtrip.
- Average rounds per session: variable — we consider 3, 8, 25 as scenario points.
- Session state hotness decay: reuse/caching reduces cost for subsequent rounds by ~15% on average because KV hits avoid recompute (very noisy).
- Chargeable unit in current API: per output token. We want to layer a session component.

Idea: Hybrid per-session credit + discounted per-token rate for the session window
- Give each session an opening fee in credits that buys the first N tokens at a higher effective discount, then per-token thereafter at base rate.
- Purpose: (1) surface cost of maintaining active sessions, (2) make short sessions cheaper per-interaction than extremely long ones, (3) control starter-credit burn.

Variant A: Session activation credits model
- Session activation = 5 credits (1 credit = equivalent of 100 tokens at baseline price for UX simplicity).
- Activation covers up to first 500 tokens of session (includes both user+model tokens). After 500 tokens, per-token billing kicks in at base rate.
- Example math (numbers simplified):
  - 1 credit = 100 tokens = $0.025 (if 1 token cost $0.00025). So 5 credits = $0.125 implicit session fee.
  - Short session (3 rounds, 60 tokens each = 180 tokens): consumes 1.8 credits -> cheaper since activation is 5 credits but we choose to deduct min(activation, tokens_consumed) logic? This is messy.

Observation: activation-as-minimum creates sticker shock for micro-interactions. Better: credits bundle purchased in packs used across sessions.

Variant B: Time-windowed session buckets (preferred sketch)
- Define session-window = 30 minutes since last user message. All rounds within window are part of same session.
- Each session gets a small flat cost (e.g., 0.5 credits) to reflect state/memory+routing overhead plus per-token charges at slightly discounted rate for the session (e.g., -10% to encourage multi-turn).
- Reconcile with starter credits: free tier gives X credits/month; small per-session fee mitigates abuse.

Scenario calcs (rough):
- Baseline per-token revenue price to customer = $0.0005/token (we charge twice our cost assume margin target).
- Cost to us = $0.00025/token. Gross margin per token = $0.00025.

Short session (3 rounds):
- Tokens = 180. Rev = 180 * 0.0005 = $0.09. Cost = 180 * 0.00025 = $0.045. Gross = $0.045.
- If we add session fee = $0.05, rev = $0.14, gross = $0.095 -> relative uplift good for economics on many short sessions.

Long session (25 rounds):
- Tokens = 1500. Rev = 1500 * 0.0005 = $0.75. Cost = 1500 * 0.00025 = $0.375. Gross = $0.375.
- If session fee applies once only, marginal impact negligible.

Break-even session fee thought: we want session fee to be meaningful for sessions < ~10 rounds, but negligible for long-running sessions. If target uplift on short sessions = +30% margin, session fee should be around $0.03-$0.08 depending on distribution.

Edge cases and abuse patterns:
- Infinite session keep-alive: clients could send pings every 29 minutes to avoid new session fee. Mitigation: require active tokens exchanged (threshold) to maintain session; idle pings don't reset window. Also rate-limit tiny messages for free tier.
- Very chatty bots: bulk per-token revenue still protects us; session fee only nudges economics.
- Long-lived contextual contexts (knowledge base) should be charged via a separate "context storage" feature (monthly) rather than per-session credits.

Open Qs / experiments to run:
- A/B test: no session fee vs 0.02 vs 0.05 vs 0.1 per activation. Track conversion on free tier -> paid, average MX tokens/session, and churn.
- Measure actual cache hit reduction per round in runtime for 1000 sample sessions to replace the 15% assumption. (Eng run: telemetry query id PRJ-1023)
- Simulation: given our user distribution (p90 rounds = 18, median = 6, mean = 12), simulate monthly revenue change under different session fees with price elasticity guesses.
- UX: how to show this to end users? "Sessions" is opaque to product designers. Consider exposing "conversation credit" meter in console that shows "credits per session" usage.

Notes to self (implementation considerations):
- Billing: simplest is to run server-side aggregator that rolls events into session windows (by user+conversation id) and emits a single session-charge event + token usage to billing pipeline daily. That avoids per-request billing latency.
- Quotas: map session-fee to free-tier quota (e.g., free tier includes 100 session activations/month + 10k tokens).
- Docs: need clear examples: "If you have 5 quick exchanges, you will use ~X credits"—build calculator + example table.

Prototype metrics to watch if we launch session fee pilot:
- Avg tokens per session, session starts per active user, free tier burn rate, conversion from free -> pay, refunds/complaints, decrease in token spam attacks.

Rough TODOs:
- [ ] Ask eng to measure real per-token cost by scenario (short/medium/long) (Ravi)
- [ ] Build simulator (Leah) against user distribution and test fee levels
- [ ] Design simple UX copy for session credits (design)
- [ ] Run small pilot with 5% of signups for 6 weeks (ops)

Conclusion: session-aware pricing can help stabilize unit economics for chat-first flows and reduce free-tier abuse. Start conservative (small fee, strong telemetry) and iterate.

Random aside: maybe call the unit "conversation credit" instead of session — feels friendlier. Make sure API naming maps to internal metric names (session_window_ms, session_activations).

End of scratchpad. Will clean and move to a product PRD if signals are good.
